toolingCaveats: SLITHER: real signal confirmed -- 89 raw results across all 5 first-party implementation contracts (29 contracts, 96 detectors). The known --filter-paths 'lib/' FALSE-CLEAN trap was avoided by anchoring the filter to the project's OWN nested lib ('phlimbo-ea-sast/lib/|phlimbo-ea-sast/test/'); zero lib/ or test/ leakage verified in the output.

SEMGREP: PARTIAL SIGNAL, NOT AN ALL-CLEAR. p/smart-contracts did load 50 Solidity rules and parsed 12/12 files at ~100%, so it is not the 'no applicable ruleset' no-op of prior runs -- but every one of its 163 findings is an INFO-level gas/performance/style rule (use-custom-error-not-require, state-variable-read-in-a-loop, use-ownable2step, ...). The ruleset contains ZERO security detectors for this code. Semgrep silence on security therefore carries no evidential weight; it contributed 0 normalized findings.
ADERYN: real signal -- 88 detectors over 12 ingested files, 1 high + 12 low issue classes (105 instances).

SOLC/BUILD PROFILE: foundry.toml changed in this range (optimizer=true, optimizer_runs=10000, via_ir=false). No finding here depends on the build profile: Slither and Aderyn analyse the AST/IR from source, not optimized bytecode, and no detector in this run is codegen- or gas-metering-sensitive. NOTE: Aderyn compiled with solc v0.8.30 while the source pragma is ^0.8.19 and solc-select was pinned to 0.8.19 for Slither -- a version skew that does not affect the detectors that fired, but is recorded for reproducibility. The via_ir=false rationale in foundry.toml is a test-harness (vm.warp) concern, not a contract-correctness one.
READ-ONLY COMPLIANCE: lib/phlimbo-ea was never written to. All tools ran against an rsync copy at the scratchpad path (.git/out/cache excluded); finding paths are normalized back to src/-relative.
